transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is… I’ve just stopped caring about almost everything I used to look forward to. It’s not like I made some big decision to quit doing things, it’s more like the interest just drained out of me.

I used to love fishing—I'd keep my gear organized, think about where I wanted to go, check the weather, all that. Now it’s just sitting in the garage untouched, and I walk past it like it belongs to somebody else. Same with my woodshop. That used to be where I’d go to clear my head, work on little projects, mess around with tools for hours. Lately, even stepping in there feels like another job, like a chore I don’t have the energy to care about.

And even with my kids… they’ll ask me to play chess, and I’ll sit there with them, but I’m not really in it. I’m just moving the pieces because I’m supposed to. I hate saying that, because I love them, but it feels like I’m going through the motions with things that used to actually mean something to me. That’s why I’m here, I think.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of at least two weeks?

I don’t know if I can answer that cleanly. “Most of the day, nearly every day” feels very exact, and I haven’t really been tracking it like that.

I mean… I know I haven’t felt like myself, and there are a lot of days where everything feels heavy or flat, but I’m not sure I’d know where to draw the line between “depressed” and just… empty, or worn down, or not caring. Some mornings are worse, some parts of the day I can kind of function because I have to, and then later it catches up with me.

So I guess I’d say I’ve felt pretty low a lot, but whether it’s most of the day every day for two weeks—I’m honestly not sure how to measure that.

Can you think back over the last few weeks—was there a period where most days, for the majority of the day, you felt down or depressed, rather than just having some low moments mixed with normal or better moods?

Yeah… I’m trying to think about it the way you’re asking, and honestly I still don’t know that I can pin it down that neatly.

It hasn’t felt like, “Oh, Monday through Friday I was depressed from morning to night,” if that makes sense. It’s more like there’s this dull, low feeling that keeps coming back, and a lot of the time it’s just there in the background. But I do still have stretches where I’m distracted or I’m dealing with something at work or at home and I’m not actively thinking, “I feel depressed right now.” So I don’t want to say yes in a way that sounds more exact than I can be.

Over the last few weeks, most days have not felt good. I can say that. There haven’t been many days where I felt normal or like myself for the whole day. But whether it’s been the majority of the day, most days… I’m not sure. It’s hard for me to separate “down” from just feeling empty or flat. Those kind of blend together for me.
Have you found that you no longer enjoy things that used to bring you pleasure, like fishing or working in your woodshop?

Yeah. That’s probably the clearest thing I can point to, honestly. I’ve just… stopped caring about the things I used to look forward to.

Fishing used to be a big deal for me. Not just going out, but all of it—getting the gear ready, checking what needed fixing, thinking about where I might go. Now the rods and tackle are just sitting in the garage, untouched. I see them there and it’s like they belong to someone else. I don’t feel pulled toward it at all.

And the woodshop is the same. That used to be my place to unwind, where I’d lose track of time working on something. Now even walking in there feels like work. Like another chore I’m supposed to do, not something I want to do.

Even with my kids asking me to play chess… I’ll do it, because I’m their dad and I don’t want to let them down, but I’m not really enjoying it. I’m just moving pieces around and trying to act normal. It feels awful to say that, but yeah, I’m mostly just going through the motions.
Have you felt a noticeable loss of energy or felt fatigued almost every day, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yeah… yes. That part is pretty noticeable. It’s not just being tired at the end of a long day, like after a normal hard day on a job site. I know what that feels like. This is different.

By midmorning, sometimes I feel like I’ve already worked a full shift, even if I haven’t done much more than get myself moving and start the day. It’s like I’m running on empty before the day has really even gotten going.

And at work, just walking the project feels heavier than it should. Climbing stairs with the crew, going from one area to another, checking on things—stuff I’ve done for years without thinking about it—now it feels like my body is carrying wet concrete. That’s the best way I can describe it. Everything takes more effort than it should, and I catch myself almost dreading the next walk-through because I know how drained I’m going to feel.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not doing anything that should wipe me out like that. But yeah, almost every day I feel worn down way earlier than I should.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… that’s changed too. I didn’t really notice it at first, because it wasn’t like I made some decision to eat less or go on a diet or anything. It was more like food just stopped seeming worth the effort.

Most days, food tastes like cardboard. That sounds dramatic, but that’s really how it feels. I’ll look at something I normally would’ve eaten without thinking, and it just has no appeal. Breakfast is the easiest thing to skip, so I usually do. I’ll tell myself I’ll grab something later, but then later comes and I still don’t really want anything.

Even after being out on a job site all day, when I know I should be hungry, I’ll sit down for dinner and just pick at it. Move it around, take a few bites, try to make it look like I’m eating more than I am. It’s not that I’m trying to lose weight. I’m not. I just don’t have much interest in food.

And yeah, my weight must’ve gone down some, because my belt’s had to come in a couple notches. I haven’t been tracking pounds or anything, but that’s hard not to notice. It’s not intentional. It just sort of happened.
Have you found yourself feeling like a failure or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not living up to who you should be?

Yeah… very much so. Probably more than I want to admit.

I keep feeling like I’ve failed everybody. My wife, my kids, the guys at work… all of them. And it’s not even always tied to some huge thing. It can be something small, like missing an appointment or forgetting to follow up on something, and my mind just grabs onto it and turns it into, “See? You can’t even handle basic things.”

At work it’s especially bad. If there’s a cost overrun, or something gets delayed, or there’s a safety issue—even if I know, logically, there are a lot of moving parts and it’s not all on one person—I still take it like it proves I’m useless. Like I shouldn’t be the one in charge. Like the crew would be better off with somebody else running things.

And at home… I feel like I’m not the husband or father I’m supposed to be. I look at my wife and kids and I just think they deserve better than this version of me. Better than someone who’s barely keeping up and constantly letting people down.

It’s like every mistake becomes evidence. I don’t just think, “I messed that up.” I think, “That’s who I am. I’m the problem.” And once that thought starts, it’s hard to get away from it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep—like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—even when you haven’t been physically or mentally exhausted?

Yeah… sleep has been pretty bad. It’s one of the worst parts, honestly, because I’ll be exhausted — like bone-tired — and I’ll think, okay, at least tonight I should just pass out. But then I get into bed and my body feels wiped out, and my head just… won’t shut off.

I’ll lie there running through everything. Bills, schedules, what’s coming up on the job, what didn’t get done, who I need to call, what might go wrong. It’s like as soon as the room gets quiet, my brain decides that’s the perfect time to start pulling out every problem and laying it on the table. I’ll look at the clock and realize an hour has gone by, then another, and that makes it worse because then I start thinking about how little sleep I’m going to get before I have to drive out to the site.

And even on nights when I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning. Just wide awake. Not rested, not ready to start the day — just awake. I’ll stare at the ceiling, maybe turn over a dozen times, try not to check the clock because I know that’ll make me more frustrated, but I always end up checking anyway.

Then I’m just lying there waiting for it to be time to get up. It’s miserable because I’m tired the whole time, but I can’t actually sleep.
Have you ever had a period like this before—where you felt this low, lost interest in things, and struggled with energy and sleep—or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I’m… not really sure how to answer that cleanly.

I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before. Everybody has, right? Times where work was heavy or things at home were stressful and I felt worn down or in a bad mood for a while. But I don’t know if I’d say it was like this. This feels… heavier, I guess. Or maybe I just didn’t pay attention before, I don’t know.

I’m trying to think back and compare it, but it’s hard because when you’re in it, everything kind of blurs together. I can remember being stressed in the past, definitely. I can remember not sleeping great during busy projects. But whether I felt this low, this consistently, with everything feeling like such a struggle… I don’t know. I can’t say for sure.

So I guess the honest answer is I don’t really know if I’ve had a period like this before. It feels different to me now, but I’m not sure if that’s because it actually is different or because I’m just noticing it more.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt so down, low, or hopeless that it affected your work, relationships, or ability to function for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… this time definitely. I mean, if you’re asking about at least two weeks, then yes, much longer than that.

It’s been going on for… about a year and seven months now, I think. It started after my wife’s health problems changed everything at home. That was kind of the point where life stopped feeling like something I was managing and started feeling like something I was just trying to survive day by day.

And it wasn’t like a bad week or a stressful month where you push through and then things settle back down. It just kept going. Weeks turned into months, and then after a while I stopped even thinking of it as a “rough patch,” because it became the way things were. Work, home, everything started feeling affected by it. So yes… it’s definitely been more than two weeks. A lot more.

I can remember not sleeping great during busy projects. But whether I felt this low, this consistently, with everything feeling like such a struggle… I don’t know. I can’t say for sure.

So I guess the honest answer is I don’t really know if I’ve had a period like this before. It feels different to me now, but I’m not sure if that’s because it actually is different or because I’m just noticing it more.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a previous major depressive episode that meets criteria, to distinguish between F32.2 (Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent) and F33.2 (Persistent Depressive Disorder, Dysthymia).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt so down, low, or hopeless that it affected your work, relationships, or ability to function for at least two weeks in a row?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and seven months, since my wife’s health problems changed everything at home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether a low or hopeless period lasted at least two weeks in a row; this maps most directly to the duration of the depressive symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… this time definitely. I mean, if you’re asking about at least two weeks, then yes, much longer than that.

It’s been going on for… about a year and seven months now, I think. It started after my wife’s health problems changed everything at home. That was kind of the point where life stopped feeling like something I was managing and started feeling like something I was just trying to survive day by day.

And it wasn’t like a bad week or a stressful month where you push through and then things settle back down. It just kept going. Weeks turned into months, and then after a while I stopped even thinking of it as a “rough patch,” because it became the way things were. Work, home, everything started feeling affected by it. So yes… it’s definitely been more than two weeks. A lot more.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a recurrent moderate depressive episode, based on the presence of persistent low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, weight loss, self-blame, and significant functional impairment lasting for over one year. The chronic and recurrent nature of the symptoms, along with the absence of a prior clear episode, supports a diagnosis of recurrent rather than a single episode.
